name: Fortran (gfortran) in fortran-lang/benchmarks: poisson2d (optimized)
baseline: C (gcc -Ofast) optimized.c: the same Jacobi-iteration Poisson solver on an MxM double grid, written as a line-by-line transliteration of optimized.f90
workload: Jacobi iteration for a 2D Poisson equation (tolerance 1e-6, grid spacing 0.01, two charged squares) on an MxM double-precision grid for M=100, 200 and 300; whole-run time in seconds.
claimed_speedup: README timings (seconds): optimized Fortran 0.18 / 6.25 / 31.4 versus optimized C 0.37 / 6.80 / 32.8 for M=100 / 200 / 300, i.e. about 1.09x faster at M=200 and 1.04x at M=300 (derived from page data). The README says the M=100 C runs did nearly double the iterations, so that column is not comparable. Naive versions go the other way: naive Fortran 0.34 / 13.2 / 69.7 versus naive C 0.42 / 7.25 / 33.7, so naive C is about 1.8-2.1x faster at M=200 and 300.
compiler_and_flags: gfortran sourcefile.f95 -Ofast and gcc sourcefile.c -Ofast (from the README); compiler versions not stated; no -march, LTO or PGO on either side.
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 3600 @ 3.6 GHz, WSL2 on Windows 10 (README)
tradeoffs: Toy 300x300 static-array Jacobi solver, not a library. Fortran needs gfortran; the repo also carries pure Python and Cython versions (Cython 229 s at M=300 versus 31-34 s for Fortran and C).
caveats: The margin is 4-9% on one machine and only for the hand-optimized pair (rho precomputed into an array); the naive pair shows naive C about twice as fast as naive Fortran, so there is no consistent language-level win. The README gives no mechanism, which caps the tier at C even though code, flags and CPU are public (compiler versions are missing). I read all four sources: the C and Fortran loops are near transliterations (inner loop over the second index, which is the strided index in column-major Fortran), but the C version swaps by copying through malloc'd pointer-to-array rows without restrict, while Fortran uses static arrays with maxval(abs()) and whole-array assignment, so aliasing and array semantics (not stated by the source) are the likely reasons. Timing is clock() in C and cpu_time in Fortran for the whole run. The README links a Fortran discourse thread (fortran-lang.discourse.group, performance-c-vs-fortran/1461) that I could not open. Last commit is March 2022, so compiler versions are probably old.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch restricted to news.ycombinator.com ('Show HN Fortran OR Julia OR Chapel OR Futhark outperforms C++ numerical kernel github benchmark -O3') returned only discussion threads with no repo; I then opened github.com/fortran-lang/benchmarks directly (guessed from the org name) and read its README and four sources. news.ycombinator.com itself is DNS-blocked in this environment, so no thread was opened.
